 Giants signed RHP Erick Mejia to a minor league contract.
 Mejia, who logged a little bench time with the Royals in 2019 and ’20, made the move to the mound in 2025 and had a 1.09 ERA in 33 innings while sitting at 95-98 mph with his fastball in the Nationals system last season. He’s currently playing winter ball in the Dominican Republic, where he’s allowed three runs in five innings. There’s a pretty good chance he’ll log major league bullpen time at some point.
 -  Matthew Pouliot

 Nationals re-signed RHP Erick Mejia to a minor league contract. 
 Mejia’s long-winding odyssey took an unexpected turn this past season as he successfully transitioned full-time to the mound, posting a respectable 4.59 ERA and 58/34 K/BB ratio over 49 innings across 45 relief appearances at three minor-league levels, finishing the year at Triple-A. The 31-year-old journeyman hasn’t appeared in the majors in nearly five years — and that was as a utility infielder. He should at least have a chance to compete for a spot in Washington’s season-opening bullpen this spring.

 Nationals re-signed OF Erick Mejia to a minor league contract. 
 Mejia last appeared in the majors with the Royals during the pandemic-shortened 2020 campaign and will return to Washington as extra organizational depth. The 29-year-old is capable of handling multiple infield and outfield spots at this juncture and might get a look in the big leagues again at some point as a super-utility specialist.

 Nationals signed INF/OF Erick Mejia to a minor league contract with an invitation to spring training. 
 The 28-year-old Mejia went 6-for-36 for the Royals between 2019 and 2020. He came in at .261/.330/.433 for the Mariners’ Triple-A club last season. he offers plenty of versatility throughout the infield and outfield, but the bat isn’t there to make him more than a 26th man.

 Mariners signed INF/OF Erick Mejia to a minor league contract. 
 Mejia appeared in 17 games for the Royals at the major-league level between 2019 and 2020, posting a subterranean .466 OPS in 42 plate appearances, before spending all of last season at Triple-A Omaha where he slashed an underwhelming .246/.317/.409 with seven homers in 228 plate appearances. He’ll bolster the Mariners’ minor-league position player depth heading into the 2022 season.

 Orioles agreed to terms with RHP Félix Bautista on a one-year contract.
 He’ll make $2.35 million, according to MLB.com’s Jake Rill. At least all of Bautista’s missed time has kept his arbitration salaries low, and the Orioles didn’t have to give much thought to non-tendering him last year even though they knew he was going to miss most or all of the season after shoulder surgery. 2027 will be his last year before free agency, and he’s definitely a question mark after struggling some in his minor league rehab and two major league appearances at the very end of last season. There’s the chance he’ll reemerge as a top-notch closer, but we wouldn’t invest heavily before seeing how he looks in spring training.
 -  Matthew Pouliot

 Red Sox agreed to terms with INF Romy Gonzalez on a one-year contract.
 He’ll make $1.65 million, according to MassLive.com’s Chris Cotillo. 2026 was a lost season for Gonzalez, as he struggled to overcome shoulder surgery and then hurt his elbow at the end of the year. However, he was impressive enough in 2025, hitting .305/.343/.483, to get himself another chance. He’ll probably be a part of Boston’s bench as a starter against left-handers.

 Red Sox agreed to terms with INF Andruw Monasterio on a one-year contract.
 The deal is worth $1.4 million, says MassLive.com’s Chris Cotillo. Monasterio started 48 games at shortstop and batted .233/.295/.371 in 107 games overall in his first season in Boston. It’s unclear if he’ll fit on to the 2027 roster with Nick Sogard, Romy Gonzalez and Anthony Seigler also batting for a utility role, but he has options left.

 Red Sox agreed to terms with OF Eli White on a one-year contract.
 According to MassLive.com’s Chris Cotillo, White will earn $1.325 million. At least for now, the Red Sox are holding on to White, Jahmai Jones and Romy Gonzalez, even though there wouldn’t seem to be room for all three right-handed bats on the bench. White hit .276/.300/.379 in 27 games after being acquired from the Braves at the trade deadline. His season ended in early September when he injured his foot in a wall collision at Fenway.
